Subject: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate | Facility: UMCG Groningen | Date: 18 February 2025

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation following prior biopsy bucket Positive. Current PSA 4.7 ng/mL. DRE reveals a palpable Nodus.

FINDINGS: The gland occupies 37.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a sharply demarcated, intensely hypointense region measuring roughly 14 mm within the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Corresponding diffusion-weighted imaging exhibits pronounced signal restriction alongside reduced ADC values. Dynamic contrast studies reveal early, localized enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Seminal vesicles remain clear. No capsular breach or suspicious nodal enlargement is observed.

IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion situated in the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Prostate volume 37.0 mL. PSA density 0.13 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.8442101.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Routine screening in November 2022 recorded a PSA reading of 3.3 ng/mL. Digital examination appeared unremarkable during that visit. Monitoring was scheduled for late 2023 to track mild lower urinary tract symptoms alongside his age.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: A subsequent assay in December 2023 yielded a PSA value of 3.6 ng/mL. COPD remained controlled via PRN salbutamol use, and his weekly cycling regimen continued uninterrupted. The rising trend coupled with recent digital rectal changes prompted a urology consultation.
